title: Derived lower shriek and $R\Gamma_c$ (finite coefficients)
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category and let $f\colon X\to Y$ admit a
compactification [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data], with chosen compactification
$X\xrightarrow{i}\bar X\xrightarrow{g}Y$ as in [sk-def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek]. The
*derived lower shriek* is

$$
Rf_!:=Rg_*\circ D(i_!)\colon D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A),
$$

with $D(i_!)$ induced levelwise by the exact extension by zero
([sk-def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek]) and $Rg_*$ the derived pushforward of
[sk-def-sfb-finite-derived-functors]. Its bounded below version
$Rf_!^+:=R^+g_*\circ D^+(i_!)\colon D^+(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)\to D^+(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$
is the restriction of $Rf_!$: there is an isomorphism
$\iota\circ Rf_!^+\cong Rf_!\circ\iota$, with $\iota$ the inclusions $D^+\subseteq D$.

$Rf_!$ is in general *not* the right derived functor $R(f_!)=R(g_*\circ i_!)$ of the
lower shriek, although $H^0(Rf_!F)=f_!F$ for a sheaf $F$ placed in degree $0$.

The *compactly supported cohomology complex* is

$$
R\Gamma_c(X/Y,-):=R\Gamma(Y,-)\circ Rf_!\colon D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A),
$$

where $R\Gamma(Y,-)=R\Gamma(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},-)$ is the right derived functor of global
sections.

proof.text:
The functors are [def-sfb-finite-derived-lower-shriek-compactification],
[def-sfb-finite-derived-lower-shriek] and [def-sfb-finite-derived-lower-shriek-plus]. The
compatibility with the inclusions is [def-sfb-finite-derived-lower-shriek-plus-compat], and
$R\Gamma$ and $R\Gamma_c$ are [def-sfb-finite-derived-global-sections] and
[def-sfb-finite-compactly-supported].

$R(g_*\circ i_!)$ would be computed by applying $g_*i_!$ to a K-injective resolution
$K\to I$. The extension by zero $i_!$ does not send injective sheaves to $g_*$-acyclic
ones, so $g_*i_!I$ need not compute $Rg_*(i_!K)$, and the two functors differ in
general. The composite $Rg_*\circ D(i_!)$ is the one built from the two adjunctions
$D(i_!)\dashv D(i^*)$ and $Rg_*\dashv Rg^!$, which is what gives $Rf_!$ a right adjoint.
In degree $0$ they agree: for a sheaf
$F$, $H^0(Rg_*(i_!F))=g_*(i_!F)=f_!F$ since $g_*$ is left exact.
